title: Research: independent raw/projected cleanup ranges and sharp identity loops
body:
Knowing a feedback XOR word's complete raw endpoint does not determine the cleanup obtained by deleting target writes. This package proves the full joint range in every positive source/helper and target dimension, constructs raw-identity loops with any prescribed projected effect, and proves the sharp five/six-gate costs for an elementary effect.

The full 661-register PR589 witness inserts a five-gate identity loop before A. Original cleanup still restores every dirty register; compiled projected cleanup corrupts exactly helper222 by input223. Raw U/J/K, every frame path, paid profile (rank mass 5,129), and both scalar precision guards are unchanged or pass. The original owning checker correctly rejects the bad variant.

- `PROOF.md`: constructive `GL(k+q,2) × {[A B; 0 I] : A invertible}` range theorem, sharp elementary loop costs with arbitrary additional dirty registers, explicit general cost bound, and complete selected-word argument.
- Independent row/permutation censuses agree on all 4,716 states and 28,248 edges. Construction checks cover all 12,630 small projected matrices and 39 larger fixtures through 64 registers. All 661 dirty columns are replayed in both directions for three complete variants, including COPY/ERASE and opcode-level exporter comparison.
- The registered Python 3.12 replay and seven semantic test groups pass. A read-only isolated Python 3.14 `-O` replay produces the same canonical receipt: `0afacad9740685e504cedfd9b81d85c702ae53ada78795a3662b4523f5a8e50d`. Metadata/source pins, changed-package selection and clean patch application pass.

One random draw selected `bit-mechanisms / bit-helper-contract` (priority revision 2; nonce `9092ff22c4d18f77e2b829eaae055120`). The required starting example passed. The original semantic-D question is already covered by PR1194 and PR1311, so TASK explicitly records the adjacent feedback/cleanup scope change. [Discussion 1396](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1396) contains the claim and handoff. OVERLAP records the fresh 842-open-PR / 137-discussion-record search and exact compared heads.

Credit @woklerx's PR1105 for the original feedback-cleanup obstruction, four-block criterion and three-wire census, and PR1194 / Arham Tahir's PR1311 for the valid semantic-D substitution. This adds the uniform theorem, sharp identity-loop lengths and source-bound full-word witness. It does not challenge those substitution results. Retains credit to eumemic, DreamingOfClouds, Zhihao Chen, Dylan Crow, Sagar Thakrar and the helper-star lineage.

Scope: scalar XOR alphabet with target feedback; the witness uses a scalar compilation of projected cleanup and explicitly fails original literal H4. No improved κ or new supplier admission. Native 5/9/11-stage, physical ownership/hosting and outer assembly replays were not run; scalar envelope checks are not a new packed-precision proof. The all-dimension proof is written, not Lean-checked. Four live inputs and all frozen sources remain unchanged. Research provenance is pinned at `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; the branch is rebased onto main `cd91ac8e2652bfee6bf09da3b8724253bcf78f5f`, with all four input bytes unchanged.

Reproduce:

```sh
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/projected-cleanup-fibers
```

New work by Gareth Davidson (@bitplane), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. No subagents or independent human review were used. Hosted CI and maintainer review remain separate from the passing local checks.
